headline: High: Dify’s writable, networked orchestration can leak or corrupt Airbyte-driven business data through shared workflows and unverified downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte can emit data over broad network egress, and Dify can ingest files and tool outputs into agent/workflow flows. If Airbyte output is routed into Dify without sanitization, prompt-like content could steer downstream instructions. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so interaction risk is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is copied into a Dify prompt or knowledge file without filtering
IF Dify treats imported content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation prompt
Strip HTML/markdown and control tokens before import
Use a read-only staging file for Airbyte exports
Manually inspect one sample payload before wiring automation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Dify reads filesystem content, handles model-provider API keys, and sends data to model providers or OpenAPI tools. In a shared workflow, business data can flow from Airbyte into Dify and then out to third parties. That creates a realistic exfiltration path in default networked deployments.
conditions: IF Airbyte exports business data into a file or API payload consumed by Dify
IF Dify forwards that content to a model provider or OpenAPI tool
mitigations: Restrict Dify inputs to redacted samples
Disable external tools for the workflow
Use separate credentials for ingestion and inference
Set short retention on uploaded knowledge files
Review one end-to-end trace for unintended fields

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can call its API and move business data; Dify can read and write files, execute shell, and spawn subprocesses. Even without git overlap, both can mutate shared workspace artifacts or downstream resources if pointed at the same directory or datastore. The concurrency model mentions shared state via Dify server datastore, so write conflicts are plausible.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path or datastore
IF Airbyte-generated artifacts are edited by Dify workflows without locking
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Add a lock file around shared artifacts
Make Airbyte outputs append-only
Run a quick conflict test on one shared record

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte produces integration data that Dify can consume in agent/workflow apps and then act on via tools. If Dify treats Airbyte output as authoritative, a bad extraction can cascade into incorrect tool calls, reports, or workflow decisions. Because Dify has action-taking authority and no verification step is guaranteed, the blast radius is potentially broad.
conditions: IF Dify uses Airbyte output as a source of truth
IF downstream tools execute based on that output without human verification
mitigations: Insert a validation step before tool execution
Require human approval for high-impact actions
Compare Airbyte output against a second source
Log and diff the exact fields passed downstream

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data, while Dify stores conversation logs and knowledge-base files and handles model-provider keys. If regulated or sensitive business data is routed into Dify, retention and residency obligations may diverge from Airbyte’s source systems. The profiles do not specify a DPA or residency controls, so the safer reading is a compliance mismatch risk rather than a proven violation.
conditions: IF regulated business data is uploaded into Dify knowledge files or conversation logs
IF retention or residency requirements differ between the source system and Dify
mitigations: Classify the data before upload
Set the shortest practical retention window
Avoid placing regulated data in conversation logs
Document the data flow and retention owner
Use a separate tenant for sensitive workloads
